column1: # exemptions.tsv (harbor#950) — every name a naming rule does not judge, and why. There are no inline ignores.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A rule that reddens a whole tree on arrival gets switched off, and a
# disabled rule protects nothing (CONSTITUTION §2.11). So the names that predate the standard are
# enumerated here, generated from each rule's own first scan of the tree, and new names are bound
# from birth. The list is decided by a person and checked, never judged at runtime.
#   tool-required  a name a tool we do not own looks up (D-1); never expires. The reason names
#   world-name     a name the world gave the thing: one row per vendored tree (D-52); never expires
#   legacy         a name from before the standard. Generated from the first scan (harbor#950,
#                  `bin/lint-name.sh --gen exemptions`), and ONLY SHRINKS: a row that no longer
#                  exempts anything is name.exemption-stale, a row added after the base is
#                  name.exemption-grow. Expires on remove_by; an expired row exempts nothing.
#                  remove_by is the date of the rename wave that retires the row (harbor#961),
#                  one batch a week, so the list never expires on one day; the reason names it.
# SUBJECT  a repo-relative path, a <register>:<name> such as env:HELM_ROOT, a directory prefix
#          ending in /, or **/<basename> for that basename at any depth (a .tmpl beside it too;
#          * in a basename matches within one segment).
# RULE     one rule id; * (every rule) only on a tool-required or world-name row.
#          No row may name standards/naming/, standards/naming.md, bin/lint-name.sh or
#          fixtures/naming/: the registry cannot exempt itself (name.exemption-self), and the
#          lint never applies a row to them.
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> rule <TAB> subject <TAB> kind <TAB> remove_by <TAB> reason
